items.headline: Futures Mixed Amid AI Stock Retreat and Rising Oil Prices
items.summary: U.S. equity futures are trading mixed early Tuesday as concerns over AI stock valuations and rising crude oil prices weigh on investor sentiment. The Nasdaq 100 futures are notably lower, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures show slight gains. This follows a mixed session on Monday where tech-heavy indices saw a rebound.

items.headline: Amazon Leads Gainers
items.summary: Amazon ($AMZN) jumped 5% on Monday, contributing to the broader tech-led rebound.

items.headline: Tesla Sees Strong Gains
items.summary: Tesla ($TSLA) climbed 3.8% in Monday's trading session.

items.headline: Nvidia Boosts S&P 500
items.summary: Nvidia ($NVDA) gained 1.4% on Monday, acting as a significant positive force for the S&P 500 due to its large market capitalization.

items.headline: AI Infrastructure Stocks Under Pressure
items.summary: CoreWeave saw a pre-market decline of 2.9% as AI infrastructure stocks slide globally due to investor concerns about debt-financed AI buildouts.

items.headline: Utilities Sector Lags
items.summary: The Utilities sector fell 2% on Monday, making it one of the day's worst-performing sectors.

items.headline: Consumer Discretionary, IT, and Materials Led Monday's Rally
items.summary: On Monday, the Consumer Discretionary, Information Technology, and Materials sectors were the strongest performers among S&P 500 sectors.

items.headline: Utilities, Real Estate, and Financials Lagged on Monday
items.summary: The Utilities, Real Estate, and Financials sectors underperformed the broader market during Monday's trading session.

items.headline: Semiconductor Stocks Face Renewed Pressure in Pre-Market
items.summary: Damage in the technology sector, particularly semiconductors, continues as chip makers and AI infrastructure groups slide in pre-market trading, driven by increasing funding difficulties for customers.

items.headline: Oil Prices Climb Amid Middle East Tensions
items.summary: Crude oil prices are higher early Tuesday, with front-month Brent crude contracts topping $110 a barrel, on track for its highest close since May 19, fueled by mounting supply risks in the Middle East.

items.headline: September Housing Data Anticipated Today
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce is set to release September housing starts at 8:30 a.m. ET, with expectations of 1.305 million units annually. Pending home sales for September are expected to be released at 10 a.m. ET, with forecasts indicating a 0.5% drop.

items.headline: Moody's Analytics Warns of 'Fiscal Reckoning'
items.summary: Moody's Analytics Chief Economist Mark Zandi issued a warning about a potential 'fiscal reckoning' for the U.S. after the Treasury Department reported a $1.992 trillion budget deficit for fiscal year 2026, driven by high outlays and increasing interest expenses.

items.headline: Netflix Earnings Expected After Market Close
items.summary: Netflix ($NFLX) is slated to report its Q3 earnings after the market closes today, with analysts expecting earnings of $0.82 per share on revenue of $12.87 billion.

items.headline: GE Aerospace and RTX Report Strong Q3 Earnings
items.summary: GE Aerospace ($GE) and RTX ($RTX) have already announced higher-than-expected Q3 adjusted earnings and revenue.
